title: River's Edge
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a Tokyo suburb in the early 1990s, high schooler Haruna protects classmate Ichiro Yamada from her boyfriend Kannonzaki's bullying, and through him meets the model Kozue. Yamada is a closeted gay student dating Kanna to appear straight; the teens' lives intertwine around a polluted riverbank until one disastrous night. A single-volume josei classic by Kyoko Okazaki, published in English by Kodansha USA.
life_message: Honest connection between damaged people matters even when adults are absent and little gets resolved.

folkways.japan: Reflects early-1990s Japanese youth culture, including compensated dating and pressure to conform, described as context.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer says the book never glosses over hurt and leaves the ending inconclusive; no moralizing reported.
delivery.note: The story observes rather than argues, leaving readers to draw conclusions.

winners_losers: No one clearly wins; Haruna and Yamada keep an unlikely friendship while others move on with little resolved, and sympathy goes to the outsiders.
